Round 28: the three open objects

Real photographs of each candidate, to pick from (answer in chat, e.g. "F3, R2, L1"). Your pick gets modelled in round 29, in the inspect view and on the floor like the lens and the gem.

FIRE: A BURNED DOLL

The doll is yours; which kind of doll it was is open. Each burns differently. (No open photograph of a burned doll exists: each kind shows the doll whole or broken, plus how its material burns.)

F1. Porcelain (bisque) doll

The glazed face blackens and crazes, the glass eyes survive; the cloth body burns away to the stuffing. A precious, kept thing.

F2. Rag doll

Cloth chars and burns through in holes, stuffing shows, button or stitched eyes. Homemade, soft, poor.

F3. Carved wooden doll

Wood chars into cracked alligator scales, the joints and pegs stay; hard, old, folk.

F4. Straw effigy

A figure made to be burned (Marzanna, wara ningyo): fire as ritual or curse, not accident.

NOTE ON THE FIRE SLOT: I found no open-licensed photograph of a real, burned doll (Commons, museum open access, Flickr, Digitalt Museum, Maryland archaeology all searched). Burned-state references available: straw effigies burning/burnt (straw), fire-char on wood with alligator cracking (wooden), broken bisque heads excavated at a fire-destroyed farmstead (bisque). Rag has no burned reference at all.

ROCK: MAGNETISM, NOT MODERN

Something about magnetism that could exist in another world.

R1. Armed lodestone

A lodestone bound in brass with iron feet and a ring, holding up an iron weight (17th-18th century). Crafted, scholarly, alchemical.

R2. Raw lodestone

A black magnetite stone with iron filings and nails standing up along its field. Natural and uncanny: a rock that pulls rocks, the field made visible.

R3. South-pointing spoon

The Han lodestone spoon turning on a bronze divination board. Ancient, a fortune-teller's tool.

R4. South-pointing fish

A thin iron fish floated in a bowl of water, turning to point south. Gentle, folk. (Only a classroom demo photo exists; no museum reconstruction found.)

## south-pointing-fish

- `south-pointing-fish/01-hmns-craft-demo.jpg`
  - page: https://blog.hmns.org/2017/02/educator-how-to-make-your-own-ancient-chinese-compass/
  - image: https://blog.hmns.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/compass1.jpg
  - licence/credit: (c) Houston Museum of Natural Science blog (rights not stated); reference use only
  - shows: WEAK: a foam-cut fish with a magnetized needle floating in an orange bowl of water. It is a classroom craft demo, not a museum reconstruction. Only image of a floating fish compass I could find.

LIFT AND BURST: NO IDEA YET

Lifts them into the air; his fist closes and they burst. My candidates.

L1. Pomegranate, split

Bursting open, seeds like blood; the underworld's fruit (Persephone). The burst.

L2. Milkweed pod

A dry pod split open, its silk seeds lifting out on the air. The lift, and letting go.

L3. Puffball

A fungus that bursts into a cloud when squeezed. The fist, and a cave thing.

L4. Hand of Sabazios

A Roman bronze votive hand raised in blessing, a snake climbing it. The gesture itself.
